title: My Happy Marriage
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In an alternate Taisho-era Japan where spirits and inherited supernatural gifts exist, Miyo Saimori, born without powers, is treated as a servant by her stepmother, half-sister and indifferent father. She is sent as a bride candidate to Kiyoka Kudo, a military commander rumored to be so cold that earlier fiancees fled within days. Instead she finds him kind, and the two slowly open their hearts in a Cinderella-style historical romance with paranormal threats; manga adaptation of a light novel.
life_message: A person's worth is not set by those who mistreat them; patient kindness and faithful love can heal deep wounds.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Family honor and bloodline prestige drive the Saimori household; Kiyoka acts out of duty, not personal feud.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Taisho-era households with clear roles and arranged marriage.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Bloodlines, inherited powers and family houses decide fate.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Powerful clans, a military commander and servant-like roles shape every relationship.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Spirits, inherited gifts and traditional customs guide life.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Safety and belonging come first; emotional expression grows slowly.

folkways.japan: Arranged marriage between great houses, ie family-line duty and Taisho-era custom are Japanese historical context; Miyo's quiet endurance (gaman) reflects valued restraint, described not judged.

winners_losers: Miyo and Kiyoka win love and security; the abusive stepmother and half-sister lose status. Sympathy goes to patient virtue and to rebuilding self-worth within tradition.
